OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '^.*\S.*$'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '^.*\S.*$'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[ \-()]*(\+[ \-()]*(\d[ \-()]*){8,15}|0[ \-()]*(\d[ \-()]*){6,13}|[1-9][ \-()]*(\d[ \-()]*){5,12})$'
          example: '0412 345 678'
        email:
          title: Email
          description: The email address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2026-09-04'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone

      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'

          properties:

              description: The ID of the pet owner.

              format: int32
              minimum: 0

              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'

## Summary

The requirement: reject creating an owner when another owner has the same `lastName` and `address` (case-insensitive, whitespace collapsed) with **409**, unless the request sets `sharesHousehold: true`.

Two files changed:

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — added a `sharesHousehold` boolean to the `OwnerFields` schema, marked `writeOnly` so it binds on the create request but never appears in responses. This makes the field available on the generated `OwnerFieldsDto` (without it, Spring's Jackson silently drops the unknown JSON property).

2. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — in `addOwner`, read the flag and extend the existing conflict guard with a household check; the matching logic lives in a tiny cohesive `sameHousehold` helper:
   ```java
   private static boolean sameHousehold(Owner a, Owner b) {
       return a.getLastName().equalsIgnoreCase(b.getLastName())
           && a.getAddress().trim().replaceAll("\\s+", " ")
               .equalsIgnoreCase(b.getAddress().trim().replaceAll("\\s+", " "));
   }
   ```

**Keeping structural impact low:** I reused the existing duplicate-detection point in `addOwner` (where the telephone-conflict 409 already lives) rather than introducing a new file or service-layer change. The comparison logic was pulled into a small, self-contained `sameHousehold` method so `addOwner` itself gained only a boolean and one extra clause — keeping both the touched function's complexity and its changed-line count minimal. Only the one method was modified plus one trivial helper, and the spec edit was unavoidable to carry the new field.
